# anomaly_schedule_preview (Data Source)

Resolves a schedule into a concrete timeline over a window: who is on call when, and where the holes are. Useful as a plan-time check that a schedule about to be attached to an escalation chain actually covers anybody.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "anomaly_schedule" "primary" {
  name = "Primary On-call"
}

data "anomaly_schedule_preview" "next_week" {
  schedule_id = data.anomaly_schedule.primary.id
  from        = "2027-01-04T00:00:00Z"
  to          = "2027-01-11T00:00:00Z"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `schedule_id` (String)

### Optional

- `from` (String) Window start (RFC3339). Defaults to the API's own window.
- `to` (String) Window end (RFC3339). Defaults to the API's own window.

### Read-Only

- `coverage_ratio` (Number) Covered fraction of the window, 0..1.
- `gaps` (Attributes List) Intervals nobody is on call for. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--gaps))
- `id` (String) Set to the schedule ID.
- `overlaps` (Attributes List) Intervals with more than one layer active. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--overlaps))
- `participants` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--participants))
- `segments` (Attributes List) Intervals with somebody on call. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--segments))
- `timezone` (String)
- `unknown_users` (List of String) Users the schedule names that no longer exist; their slots page nobody.
- `warnings` (List of String)
